entry.title: Flux v1.5 — A redesign and temperature alerts
entry.summary: Flux now has the same window design as Prisma and Mixtape, and it can warn you about GPU temperature and hot-spot temperature as well as VRAM. Just replace your old Flux.exe; your settings and leak log carry over.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.14.1

In Cyber it is a night city: a neon horizon, a synthwave…

entry.title: Prisma v2.1.0 — Redesigned main window
entry.summary: The old header is gone: a borderless title strip is the window caption now — the logo (About), the power button, a "now lighting" card (what the lights are doing… The body is two cards: a rail with your devices and profiles, and one page with Effects, Color, the live preview and Tuning. Every effect has its own small picture, shown on the effect tiles, on each device (what that device really runs) and on each profile.

entry.summary: The VRChat room widget opens right on the watch: tap it and it grows into the list of who is in the world, your friends, how long you have been there and who left… The Hexpad widget opens on the watch too: tap it and it grows into the whole dock - keys to press, knobs to drag and the page you are on.

entry.summary: The watch's volume now works with Virtual Desktop's speakers. That device ignores Windows' own volume (the Windows slider does nothing there either), so the watch sets… The Microphone widget works with Virtual Desktop's microphone.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.11.0
entry.summary: Each widget on the watch can have its own design: Tint, Solid, Two-tone, Header, Outline or Glass, or the normal card. Pick a colour for each widget: Auto or one of 13 colours. Two-tone also takes a second colour, or makes a matching one for you. In the watch layout editor, select a widget to see the Style and Colour choices with small previews. "Use on all widgets" copies the look to the whole face.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.10.1
entry.summary: The first start after updating to 1.10.0 stopped with an error while switching your colours to Bento. Fixed; your settings were not changed by it. The "What's new" window also lists what 1.10.0 brought (the new Bento look), since that version never got to show it.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.10.0
entry.summary: The watch is redesigned (Modern style; the Windows 95 style is unchanged):

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.9.4
entry.summary: While you hold the trigger on a screen, that screen keeps your laser even past its edge. The cursor stays on the edge, so dragging a window to the very top of a monitor… The other hand can no longer take the mouse in the middle of a drag. Before, the mouse jumped to the other laser when the dragging one went past the edge or held still.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.9.3
entry.summary: After an update, a "What's new" window lists what changed since your old version. In VR it appears in front of you. You can grab it and scroll it with the stick. On the desktop it appears over the settings window.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.9.2
entry.summary: The watch's volume widget controlled the Windows default device for the "multimedia" role, and only looked for a new one every 5 seconds. When Virtual Desktop made… It now follows the same default device the Windows volume icon uses, checks it every second and switches at once. The log names the device it controls, and says so if a device refuses or ignores a new level.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.9.1
entry.summary: OrbitOverlay used to update once per game frame. Measured with VRChat on a 90 Hz headset, that was 63-83 times a second, while SteamVR presented 75-85 frames. Whenever… It now runs on its own high-resolution clock at the headset's refresh rate (measured: 90 ticks/s, 0.23 ms spread). Every frame SteamVR shows, reprojected ones included… It no longer pauses for ~35 ms when SteamVR doesn't signal a frame in time.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.9.0
entry.summary: Point at the lower part of a monitor or mirrored window and a bar appears under it. It has a Theater button and theater mode's settings: Dim (how dark the world gets)… In theater mode the bar under the big screen has the same settings, which apply live. You can still switch monitors and exit from there. The same settings are under Settings > Layouts > Theater mode. You can also turn the bar off there.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.8.2
entry.summary: The big screen always goes in front of the middle of your monitors, whichever one plays. The middle monitor grows out of its place. One off to the side fades in where the big screen is, with a slight zoom, and fades out there when you leave; it no longer… Switching monitors is a real cross-fade: the new one fades in over the old one, which stays solid underneath until it is covered, so the world no longer shows through…

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.8.1
entry.summary: Theater mode: the screen shows up where your monitors are. 1.8.0 put it where you were looking when you tapped the button, which is always the watch. Lying back with… The dim behind the theater screen is now a wall just behind the screen, bent around you. Before, it was a sheet right in front of your eyes, which SteamVR could draw… The watch animates at your headset's refresh rate (it was capped at 45 fps).

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.8.0
entry.summary: A new Theater watch button: the monitor or window you used last becomes one big curved screen in front of you (2.8 m wide at 2.5 m by default). The other panels and the… Grab it to move it, the stick or both hands to size it; it stays curved around you at any distance. Point at the screen and a switcher shows up under it: one button per monitor and mirrored window to swap what plays (they cross-fade in place), and Exit.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.5.0 — Your own watch face
entry.summary: New: a custom watch face of widgets. Settings > Wrist > Watch face: Custom, then Edit layout.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.4.0 — Windows 95 style
entry.summary: New: an optional Windows 95 style. Settings > Look > Style: Modern (default, as before) or Windows 95. It switches instantly and can be switched back the same way.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.3.3 — Settings stay private
entry.summary: Opening Orbit's settings panel no longer counts as "an overlay is open" for VRChat avatar parameters. Avatar add-ons such as DXOverlay now react only to real overlays …

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.3.2 — A watch that stays put
entry.summary: Wrist > Lock position: the grip no longer moves or resizes the watch, so you can't nudge it by accident while grabbing something else. Gripping a locked watch gives a…

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.3.1 — Says hello after an update
entry.summary: If you're on 1.3.0, open Settings > General, press Check for updates, then Update to 1.3.1. Orbit downloads this release, checks it, installs it over itself and starts again - your settings and shortcuts stay as they are.

entry.title: OrbitOverlay v1.3.0 — Your desktop in orbit
entry.summary: Orbit is a lightweight SteamVR overlay for Windows: a watch on your wrist, your monitors - or single app windows - as curved screens around you with a laser mouse, a full VR keyboard, and a settings panel you can grab in VR.

entry.title: Mixtape v0.21.0 — Something hidden
entry.summary: The first iPods hid a game. Windows 95 hid its credits. This version of Mixtape hides a few things of its own — they're not in any menu, and these notes won't tell you where they are.

entry.title: Mixtape v0.20.0 — Lyrics on the iPod
entry.summary: Click-wheel iPods (Classic, nano, 5G) can show a song's lyrics while it plays — press the centre button. Mixtape now puts them there.

entry.title: Mixtape v0.19.0 — A Windows 95 look, Listening page, PC play counts
entry.summary: The headline is a whole second look for the app: Windows 95, switchable in Settings › Appearance › Look. Around it, a Listening page, play counts for your own files, and a motion pass for the modern look.

entry.title: Prisma v2.0.0 — Unified Windows RGB control
entry.summary: One app for the motherboard, RAM, GPU, fan strips, keyboard and mouse — driven from a single 25 fps frame loop so everything actually animates in step. No vendor suite, no cloud, no telemetry, no account.

entry.title: Flux v1.4 — UI refresh + a much faster process list
entry.summary: The process list used to reopen a fresh performance-counter query on every single tick. Measured on ~390 processes, the RAM view went from 36 ms to 6.9 ms per refresh — and because that work ran on the UI thread, that stall is what made the window feel sticky. The GPU counters and the CPU/DISK…
